- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently overpredicts in early 30-day horizon (days 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; reduce first 3–5 days by 0.5–1.5%.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative (e.g., drops below 0.2) mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.0) followed by 3–5 days of low sentiment: model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
